analysis.title: 10 Charts We're Talking About
key_insights: Megacap earnings disappointed (Tesla cutting capex, Meta's AI spending raising cost concerns, Lam Research guidance underwhelming), which reignited concerns about the durability of the AI trade.

Before the weakness, hedge funds had shorted heavily and sold tech at a record pace. GS prime data as of 19 Oct showed the largest two-week net selling of Global Info Tech in its 10y+ record (-3.3 std dev), with short leverage at the 99th percentile on a 5-year view.

Lower-rated borrowers' credits have been the center of the stress, as the market reassesses the economics of the AI buildout under potentially higher-for-longer long-term rates and energy cost pressures.

GS strategists remain underweight USD IG Tech and neutral USD HY. They expect dispersion across AI-related issuers to stay high, particularly in project finance bonds, where data centers (including chip/compute financing) dominate USD IG and HY project finance issuance.

Brent hit fresh local highs after Middle East headlines: US and Israel drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after elections (NYT), US diplomats ordered out of Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes, and Saudi Aramco telling staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have become more frequent over October.

USD rates remain better bid despite the oil and inflation risk. GS suspects the market treats the NYT report as unconfirmed and deniable, while the AI de-rating (credit stress in neoclouds/hyperscalers, semis weakness) looks more sustained. Real yields are driving.

French bond stress is intensifying as lawmakers grapple with the debt burden amid cost-of-living riots. The 10y OAT/Bund spread is the widest since the euro's introduction, and the absolute yield is higher than during the Eurozone crisis.

GS strategists see energy price relief as the clearest route to tighter French spreads: it improves the growth and deficit risk skew, allows limited ECB tightening to be priced, and lower rates volatility encourages carry strategies. Without it, they expect wider spreads and more pressure on EUR FX.
There has been demand for EURUSD downside, with vol still low on a long-term lookback. Investors see the discount in EUR versus USD real yield differentials as a valuation cushion for hedges.

Overlay-hedge interest is also in USDJPY puts. JPY screens about 40% undervalued versus the USD on long-term fair value models, and Japan is a clear case of outsized investment in US financial assets.

If AI concerns spiral into US-unexceptionalism and US-Japan rate differentials compress, GS expects sustained repatriation from the US to Japan (USD selling, JPY buying). Japanese officials favor a strong JPY, PM Takaichi wants more domestic investment, and the BoJ is expected to keep hiking gradually.

Equities-down / yields-down dual binaries continue to trade as growth shock hedges, and GS likes this implementation. Realized correlations recently flipped back to AI down, 10y yields lower and USD softer versus JPY.
